Turning to the quarter, consolidated service revenue grew 3.1% year on year, helped by a strong postpaid net add performance in our home market and a recovery in roaming volumes as cross border travel normalised. We added roughly 184,000 postpaid subscribers, our best Q2 in five years, and ARPU in the segment lifted about 2.4% on tariff actions taken in late March. Enterprise revenue was a softer story, declining around 1.8% as two large logistics customers reduced their fleet telemetry spend ahead of contract renewals in September. We are cautiously optimistic that most of that volume returns, but we are watching it closely given those two accounts together represent close to 4% of group service revenue. Free cash flow conversion came in at 71% of EBITDA, a bit below our 75% target, largely because of working capital build for the new 5G core buildout in the Andean region.

During the second quarter, the Group's Las Americas pit experienced a 38 metre slope displacement following an extended period of unseasonal rainfall, which forced a temporary curtailment of haulage from the higher-grade west face. Geotechnical consultants have revised the pit design parameters and the Company expects to resume full production by late Q3, although mill feed for the balance of the year will be drawn primarily from lower-grade stockpiles. The lost production, combined with the cost of the redesign and the additional waste movement required to access stable ground, is expected to weigh on unit cash costs and full year EBITDA. Beyond the immediate incident, the broader San Lorenzo district has recorded its wettest wet season in fourteen years, raising questions about the long term adequacy of the Company's water management infrastructure and tailings storage capacity assumptions.

The Company designs custom radio-frequency front-end modules for four smartphone OEMs, which together accounted for 84% of FY2024 revenue of USD 1.9 billion. Three of these customers operate dual-sourcing strategies and have provided written notifications reserving the right to qualify alternative suppliers upon any 90-day delivery miss. The Company holds USD 312 million of accounts receivable as of 30 September 2024, with the largest single customer representing USD 127 million, of which USD 41 million is more than 75 days past due. The customer's purchasing entity, headquartered in Shenzhen, has publicly disclosed liquidity constraints and is currently restructuring a USD 680 million syndicated facility with its bank group. In addition, the Company's 7nm Wi-Fi 7 FEM roadmap relies on a gallium arsenide heterojunction process available from only two foundries globally, neither of which has committed volume capacity beyond Q2 2026. A competing silicon-on-insulator approach under development by a Tier-1 handset OEM could materially displace GaAs content per handset beginning in calendar 2027.

During the quarter, the Company continued to execute its approved capital programme of approximately GBP 1.4 billion for the 2024 to 2028 regulatory period, with around 38% of spend ringfenced for wastewater treatment upgrades across the southern coastal catchments. Ofwat's final determination for AMP8 reduced the Company's allowed return on regulated equity to 3.96% and tightened the cost of debt pass-through, which we expect to compress operating margin by roughly 110 basis points in the early years of the period. The Company has lodged a formal reference with the Competition and Markets Authority challenging certain assumptions used in the PR24 methodology, and outcomes remain uncertain. Demand volumes across our metered and measured household base were 1.8% below management expectations, driven by milder summer weather and the cumulative effect of customer-side leakage reduction campaigns. We have also identified a legacy billing platform anomaly, now under investigation, that has resulted in approximately 23,000 customers being undercharged by an average of GBP 14 per month, representing a recoverable but delayed cash inflow that the Company expects to spread over the next 18 to 24 months.

I want to provide an update on our Alaska North Slope operations, where an extended cold snap in late January forced a partial shutdown of the central processing facility for eleven days. Production averaged about 142,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day during the quarter, roughly 8,000 below our pre-event guidance, and we incurred approximately $26 million in unscheduled operating and remediation expense, of which a portion is expected to be recoverable under our property insurance program subject to the customary deductible and coverage limits. We continue to engage with the regulator on the restart sequence and on additional integrity inspections that were added to the work scope. Looking ahead, we expect first quarter 2026 volumes to be modestly impacted by the deferred work and by the natural decline curve at Prudhoe, and we are assessing whether to initiate a supplementary drilling campaign later this year to partially offset the decline.

Catastrophe reinsurance pricing for the Atlantic hurricane season tightened materially during the second quarter, with treaty renewals repriced upward by 18% to 22% and aggregate attachment points raised by our reinsurers. The Group retains a 6% net share of its homeowners book after retrocession, and while the purchased program restored its $1.4 billion per-occurrence limit, several layer providers required collateralization terms that will consume an additional $90 million of statutory capital if the named storm count exceeds seven in the third quarter. We expect the ceded premium ratio to remain elevated through year end, and management has scaled back writings in coastal Florida and the Carolinas, which together produced 31% of gross premium last year, to preserve margin against an above-normal outlook issued by the National Hurricane Center.

The Company relies on a single regional jet engine manufacturer for the heavy maintenance, repair and overhaul of the CFM56-7B powerplants installed across its 38-aircraft narrowbody fleet, and any insolvency, prolonged labor disruption or quality-related production halt at that supplier could ground a substantial portion of the fleet within sixty to ninety days given the absence of a qualified alternative MRO provider at comparable turnaround times.

The Group's sugar refining operations are subject to quota and tariff regulation in its principal end-markets, including the European Union and the United Kingdom, where preferential access arrangements are subject to periodic renegotiation. Any material reduction in the Group's quota allocation, or the imposition of additional duties on refined sugar imports, could erode margins on shipments to these destinations and may require the Group to redirect volumes to lower-margin domestic or spot channels. Currency translation also affects reported results, as a significant portion of revenue is denominated in pounds sterling and euros while input cane costs are substantially settled in U.S. dollars.

The Group has entered into forward foreign exchange contracts to hedge between 50% and 75% of forecast net receivables for the upcoming twelve months, but residual unhedged exposure remains. Movements in the sterling and euro against the dollar outside the range assumed in the Group's planning assumptions could reduce reported EBITDA and affect compliance with the financial covenants set forth in the Indenture governing the Notes.

The Group's freight forwarding operations in the Black Sea and Eastern Mediterranean corridors are subject to elevated geopolitical instability, including the continuing armed conflict in Ukraine, periodic disruption to commercial shipping in the Turkish Straits, and the imposition of new sanctions packages by the European Union, the United Kingdom and the United States. Sanctions have required repeated screening of counterparties, vessel beneficial ownership, and cargo descriptions, and any designation of additional ports, carriers or beneficial owners could force the rerouting or cancellation of booked shipments. We have, on occasion, been unable to obtain documentary confirmation of cargo insurance coverage for transits through conflict-adjacent waters, which has led to declined bookings and unrecovered demurrage charges at Constanța and Piraeus. Should geopolitical conditions deteriorate further, the Group may be required to suspend services on additional trade lanes, with a corresponding reduction in forwarding volumes that we currently estimate at between 4% and 7% of segment revenue.

The Company's commercial loan portfolio is concentrated in middle-market manufacturing, agribusiness and energy-related borrowers across the Midwest, and a sustained downturn in commodity prices or regional agricultural yields could simultaneously impair borrower cash flows, reduce collateral coverage on revolving credit facilities and elevate net charge-offs. Approximately 38% of outstanding balances mature or reprice within twelve months, exposing earnings to a steeper yield curve and to potential asset-liability mismatch if deposit pricing adjusts more slowly than wholesale funding costs. The allowance for credit losses methodology relies on macroeconomic forecasts produced by third-party vendors, and prolonged deviation between forecast and realized unemployment or GDP could require larger provisions in subsequent quarters, compressing return on equity.

The Group's property management platform relies on a single integrated enterprise system, supplied under a long-term licence by a major European software vendor, which handles tenant billing, lease accounting, rent collection and the production of regulatory and Noteholder reporting. A material failure of, or prolonged interruption to, that system, whether arising from a vendor product defect, a cybersecurity incident, an inability of the vendor to continue support, or a failure of the Group to migrate to the vendor's successor cloud platform by the contractual cut-over date in 2027, could disrupt rent collection, delay financial reporting and give rise to breaches of covenants and reporting undertakings under the Indenture. The Group is currently in user-acceptance testing of the successor platform; however, the migration has already experienced scope changes and a four month delay relative to the original timetable. Any inability to complete the migration on a timely basis, or to operate effectively on the legacy system during a transition period, may also necessitate engagement of specialist consultants at additional cost.

Let me move to the macro picture and a couple of items that we are tracking closely. Electricity is now our single largest controllable opex line, and we have layered in additional hedging through to the second quarter of next year, but our tariff unit cost is still running about 18 percent higher than the prior comparable period, so any sustained upward move in wholesale power markets beyond our hedge envelope will feed directly into operating cost. We are also watching the evolving sanctions environment around a small set of specialty chemical inputs sourced from Eastern European producers; while our direct exposure is modest, one of our key dosing polymer suppliers has flagged that a particular precursor is now subject to an export licensing regime, which could lengthen lead times by four to eight weeks. Lastly, we are mid-implementation of a new customer billing platform, and the data migration has been more complex than the vendor originally scoped, which has us tracking a six to ten week go-live slip versus the original plan.
